entities.summary:
Barses (b. 350 CE) was a successful entrepreneur and business leader of the Classical era, active in the Global region. A prominent religious figure, Barses played a significant role in the development of religious institutions and practices during this period.

Barses was a key figure in the establishment of several religious organizations, including the Church of Alexandria, which became a major center of Christianity. Through his business acumen and strategic partnerships, Barses helped to expand the reach of these organizations and facilitated the spread of religious ideas across the Mediterranean world.

The legacy of Barses can be seen in the continued influence of Christianity on Western civilization, as well as the development of new religious movements and sects that emerged during the Classical era. His contributions to the growth and spread of religious institutions also laid the groundwork for the complex and diverse religious landscape of the Middle Ages.

Despite the passage of centuries, Barses remains an important figure in the annals of Christian history, and his impact on the development of religious institutions and practices continues to be felt today.
